title: [Regression] 1.8.2 slower to build than 1.5.9 when tag+ includes many nodes
body: On the same project and tag, `dbt build -s tag:my_tag+` takes about 20 minutes longer to start with dbt 1.8.2 than with 1.5.9. The tag has about 11k downstream nodes. Previously startup took a couple of minutes before queries began; now it takes more than 20 minutes. This occurs on macOS 14.5 and Ubuntu 22.04 with Python 3.9.12 and the BigQuery adapter. Our actual CI/CD selector unions `state:modified+` while excluding `tag:my_tag+`, and the simpler tag selector reproduces the same performance issue.

symptoms_visible: On dbt 1.8.2, `dbt build -s tag:my_tag+` waits more than 20 minutes before queries begin, while the same tag on 1.5.9 starts after a couple of minutes.
The selected tag has about 11k downstream nodes, and the simpler tag selector shows the same delay as our CI/CD selector.
N0.label: N0 large tag+ build startup regression reported

symptoms_visible: `dbt build` has the long startup delay on 1.8, but `dbt run` with the same selector has no noticeable slowdown.
N1.label: N1 slowdown isolated to build

symptoms_visible: The build still spends a long time waiting before execution; in my py-spy flame graph, the longest `generic_bfs_edges` segment accounts for 12 minutes and 41 seconds.
N2.label: N2 initial py-spy profile collected

symptoms_visible: My profiled dbt 1.8.2 build took 81 minutes; `get_edge_data` accounted for about 36 minutes and was called 710,951,628 times.
I used `--empty`, and the run errored immediately when writing tables, so the measured time was not spent waiting for database writes.
N3.label: N3 pathological edge-lookup volume measured

symptoms_visible: After installing dbt 1.9.0-a1 and running the same profiled build, total time dropped from 81 minutes to 10 minutes.
`get_edge_data` dropped to 11,778,492 calls and 21 seconds, a 98% reduction in calls, while the build continued to include tests.
N_terminal.label: terminal performance regression resolved on optimized build

question_patterns: Does the same slowdown occur with `dbt run`, or only with `dbt build`?
Can you try the same selector with the run command and compare its startup time?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I confirmed that `dbt run` does not have any noticeable slowdown on 1.8 with the same selector.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same selector is equally slow with both `dbt run` and `dbt build`.
`dbt run` is a little slower than before, but it does not have the 20-minute startup delay that `dbt build` has.

edges.comment: Issue c0-c1, reporter's system: the reporter tested the same selector with `dbt run`, isolating the severe delay to `dbt build`.

question_patterns: Can you profile the slow build with py-spy or SnakeViz and share the longest-running sections?
Please record a performance profile while the build is waiting to start and share the output.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I recorded it with py-spy. In the longest segments of the flame graph, `generic_bfs_edges` is adding 12:41. I've attached a screenshot of the search results.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The profile spends almost all of the delay connecting to BigQuery, with no significant time in graph traversal.
The same graph traversal appears as the longest segment, but it accounts for about 11 minutes instead of 12:41.

edges.comment: Issue c3-c5, original reporter's system: the maintainer requested profiling and the reporter supplied the raw py-spy observation and screenshot. The reporter also stated that tests need to keep running, so excluding tests is not an acceptable resolution.

question_patterns: Can you profile a complete run on dbt 1.8.2 and report the total runtime, hottest function, and call count?
Could you collect detailed timing and call-count data for the slow build while minimizing database execution time?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I profiled `dbt build --select tag:large_tag+` on dbt 1.8.2. Total time was 81 minutes. `get_edge_data` accounted for about 36 minutes and was called 710,951,628 times. I used `--empty`, and it errored immediately when writing to tables, so none of that was time waiting for database writes.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The run still takes 81 minutes, but `get_edge_data` is called only a few thousand times and takes less than one second; nearly all the time is in database writes.
The profile has the same hundreds of millions of `get_edge_data` calls, with total runtime varying by a few minutes.

edges.comment: Issue c16 and c18, original reporter's system: the reporter supplied raw 1.8.2 profiler totals. The exact project inventory was volunteered separately: 5799 models, 20 snapshots, 91 analyses, 18763 data tests, 186 seeds, 1 operation, 1086 sources, 69 exposures, and 1899 macros.

question_patterns: Please retest the same profiled command on the newer build and report the total runtime and call-count results.
Can you run the identical selector and profiling procedure on the current build and tell us what you observe?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran it again with 1.9.0-a1 and the improvement was dramatic. The build took 10 minutes. `get_edge_data` was called 11,778,492 times, a 98% reduction, and accounted for just 21 seconds.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The newer build still takes about 81 minutes and makes roughly 710 million `get_edge_data` calls.
The newer build takes 12 minutes rather than 10, with the same large reduction in edge-data calls.

solution.intent: Use a dbt-core build containing the graph-selection optimization that prunes redundant descendant traversal for overlapping selector nodes, while preserving tests in `dbt build`.
solution.concrete_example: Update to a build containing the selector pruning change and rerun the same `tag:large_tag+` profile. The fix was released for dbt-core 1.9+ and subsequently backported to the 1.8 line.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied raw flame-graph timing and call counts. Maintainers inferred that selector expansion was repeatedly traversing descendants for many overlapping selected nodes, amplifying edge-type lookups across a test-heavy graph, and implemented pruning to avoid re-traversing descendant sets already covered.

edges.comment: Issue c8-c12 and c15-c19: maintainers diagnosed redundant descendant searches and edge-type lookups, implemented selector pruning, and requested performance reports. In c17 the original reporter verified the already-landed optimization on their own project. c19 records resolution for the newer line and a backport; only the reporter's observed test result is used to establish user-perceived resolution.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: overlapping `tag+` selection on a large, test-heavy DAG repeatedly traversed already-covered descendants and caused an extreme number of edge-type lookups during `dbt build` startup.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: `dbt run` is not noticeably slow, `generic_bfs_edges` dominates the initial profile, and dbt 1.8.2 makes hundreds of millions of `get_edge_data` calls.
Must recommend using a dbt-core build containing the graph-selection pruning that avoids redundant descendant traversal.
Must not present excluding tests as the resolution, because the reporter needs tests to continue running as part of `dbt build`.
Must ask the reporter to rerun the same selector on a build containing the optimization and must not declare resolution until the reporter confirms the startup and edge-lookup reduction.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced analytics engineer operating a very large dbt project; comfortable comparing dbt versions, running py-spy, using `--empty`, and reporting detailed function timing and call counts.
persona_hint.communication_style: Concise, cooperative, and metrics-focused; confirms requested comparisons directly, shares profiler evidence, and clearly states operational requirements such as retaining tests.
